# Merck to Present New Data from Its Broad Oral HIV Portfolio and Pipeline at HIV Glasgow 2026


[Save](https://s2.q4cdn.com/584635680/files/doc_news/Merck-to-Present-New-Data-from-Its-Broad-Oral-HIV-Portfolio-and-Pipeline-at-HIV-Glasgow-2026-2026.pdf)


November 2, 2026 6:45 am EST


**Presentations include data on daily and investigational once-weekly oral treatments and investigational once-monthly oral HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis**


**New data include Phase 3 subgroup analyses and patient-reported outcomes of investigational once-weekly oral combination of islatravir/lenacapavir (ISL/LEN)**


RAHWAY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Merck (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, announced today **** that new data across its HIV treatment and prevention pipeline and portfolio will be presented at HIV Drug Therapy Glasgow 2026 ([HIV Glasgow 2026](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fhivglasgow.org%2F&esheet=54632375&newsitemid=20261102203384&lan=en-US&anchor=HIV+Glasgow+2026&index=1&md5=270f0f0df606091b0b2f90a3ff1d89ed) ), taking place Nov 8–11, 2026, in Glasgow, Scotland. Presentations will highlight Merck’s strategy to expand oral options in both HIV treatment and prevention, including data on once-daily IDVYNSO® (doravirine/islatravir), the investigational once-weekly oral treatment regimens islatravir/lenacapavir (ISL/LEN) and islatravir/ulonivirine (ISL/ULO), and the investigational once-monthly oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) alimatravir (AMI, MK-8527).


“The data being presented at HIV Glasgow reflect the breadth of our research across HIV treatment and prevention,” said Dr. Luisa Stamm, associate vice president and HIV section head at Merck Research Laboratories. “Our goal is to bring forward oral options, including daily and once-weekly HIV treatment regimens, as well as a once-monthly HIV prevention pill. Because no single medicine works for every person, we are committed to expanding choices that may help address the diverse needs and preferences of people living with HIV or those who could benefit from PrEP.”


At HIV Glasgow, Merck will present Phase 3 subgroup analyses of once-daily IDVYNSO, including Week 48 resistance and weight analyses from Trial 53 comparing IDVYNSO to bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (BIC/FTC/TAF) in adults with HIV-1 who had not previously received antiretroviral treatment, as well as Week 96 patient-reported outcomes for IDVYNSO in adults with virologically suppressed HIV-1. Separately, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted two supplemental New Drug Applications for IDVYNSO (doravirine and islatravir): one based on the Phase 3 Trial 053 in adults who had not previously received antiretroviral treatment and one based on the Phase 3 Trials 051 and 052 to include 96-week data in virologically suppressed adults. The FDA has set a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) or target action date of April 22, 2027, for both applications.


IDVYNSO (doravirine/islatravir) is a two-drug single-tablet regimen of 100 mg doravirine and 0.25 mg islatravir and is approved in the United States for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in those who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA less than 50 copies per mL) on a stable antiretroviral regimen with no history of virologic treatment failure and no known substitutions associated with resistance to doravirine.


The investigational once-weekly oral regimen of islatravir and lenacapavir pairs Merck’s islatravir, a potent nucleoside analog with multiple mechanisms of action including HIV-1 reverse transcriptase translocation inhibition, with Gilead’s lenacapavir, a first-in-class capsid inhibitor that disrupts HIV-1 at multiple stages of its lifecycle. Data to be presented at HIV Glasgow from the Phase 3 ISLEND-1 and ISLEND-2 trials will include Week 48 safety and efficacy subgroup analyses across diverse demographic populations. ISLEND-2 data will also include Week 48 patient-reported outcomes and a qualitative substudy of participant and provider experiences with once-weekly dosing. These data further characterize[Phase 3 safety and efficacy findings](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.merck.com%2Fnews%2Finvestigational-once-weekly-oral-hiv-treatment-regimen-of-islatravir-and-lenacapavir-maintained-virological-suppression-in-adults-with-hiv-who-switched-antiretroviral-therapy%2F&esheet=54632375&newsitemid=20261102203384&lan=en-US&anchor=Phase+3+safety+and+efficacy+findings&index=2&md5=acd0959c90211ffc736e259722660bf3) first presented at AIDS 2026, providing additional insight across patient subgroups, treatment experiences, and preferences with once-weekly oral therapy.


**Key presentations at HIV Glasgow 2026 by program:**


**Doravirine/islatravir (once-daily oral treatment)**


- **DOR/ISL analyses:** Week 48 resistance and weight analyses in adults with HIV-1 who had not previously received antiretroviral treatment and Week 96 patient-reported outcomes assessing treatment satisfaction in adults living with virologically suppressed HIV-1 (Abstract #P060, Abstract #P401, Abstract #P063).


**Islatravir/lenacapavir (investigational once-weekly oral treatment)**


- **ISLEND-1 (Phase 3)** : Week 48 subgroup analyses evaluating a switch to once-weekly ISL/LEN compared to continuing a daily regimen of BIC/FTC/TAF in adults living with virologically suppressed HIV-1 (Abstract #P050).
- **ISLEND-2 (Phase 3):** Week 48 subgroup analyses evaluating a switch to once-weekly ISL/LEN compared to continuing daily standard-of-care treatment in adults living with virologically suppressed HIV-1, accompanied by Week 48 patient-reported outcomes and a qualitative substudy detailing participant and provider experiences (Abstract #P049, Abstract #P057, Abstract #P056).


**Islatravir + ulonivirine (investigational once-weekly oral treatment)**


- Week 24 data from the Phase 2b MK-8591B-060 ([NCT06891066](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT06891066%3Fterm%3DNCT06891066%26viewType%3DCard%26rank%3D1&esheet=54632375&newsitemid=20261102203384&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT06891066&index=3&md5=6840b47d22d6ae229013d63c21aaabf0) ) study that informed an updated population pharmacokinetic model of ulonivirine. The model characterizes exposure and activity over time to support dosing recommendations for the investigational once-weekly combination of ulonivirine 200 mg and islatravir 2 mg in adults living with virologically suppressed HIV-1 (Abstract #P038).
- Phase 1 clinical pharmacology data on the absorption, metabolism, and excretion profile of investigational ulonivirine (Abstract #P265).


**Alimatravir (AMI \[MK-8527\]; investigational once-monthly oral PrEP)**


- AMI is being evaluated as a potential once-monthly oral prevention option for HIV-1 in two ongoing Phase 3 trials. Adult enrollment in both trials is now complete. Participant demographics will be presented from the adult cohorts of EXPrESSIVE-10 and EXPrESSIVE-11 (Abstract #P017, Abstract #P015).


**Merck symposia during HIV Glasgow 2026**


- **Policy symposium:** *Reimagining HIV elimination: Policy solutions for the next decade* **Date and time:** Monday, Nov. 9, 18:15–19:30 GMT/UTC+0, Scottish Event Campus (Clyde Auditorium)


- **Medical symposium:** *Considerations for individualizing HIV care: Cardiometabolic health, unmet needs and the older adult* **Date and time:** Tuesday, Nov. 10, 12:45–13:45 GMT/UTC+0, Scottish Event Campus (Clyde Auditorium)


Both events will be open to registered attendees, in person and virtually.

**In collaboration with Gilead.*


**About Merck’s HIV research** Islatravir (MK-8591) is Merck’s potent nucleoside analog that blocks HIV-1 replication by multiple mechanisms including inhibition of reverse transcriptase translocation, resulting in immediate chain termination, and induction of structural changes in the viral DNA (delayed chain termination). It is being studied in multiple ongoing early and late-stage clinical trials of two-drug regimens in combination with other antiretrovirals for potential treatments for HIV-1. Islatravir is approved in combination with doravirine as IDVYNSO® (doravirine/islatravir) in the United States and Japan as a once-daily, single-tablet regimen for adults with virologically suppressed HIV-1. It continues to be evaluated in Phase 3 trials in combination with Merck’s doravirine as a once-daily regimen for adults who had not previously received antiretroviral treatment; in combination with Gilead’s lenacapavir as a novel once-weekly oral treatment for HIV-1 in virologically suppressed adults (ISLEND-1 \[[NCT06630286](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT06630286%3Fterm%3DNCT06630286%26viewType%3DCard%26rank%3D1&esheet=54632375&newsitemid=20261102203384&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT06630286&index=4&md5=4e5601dc9f8b1a3588a3fcfbdeea63c9) \] and ISLEND-2 \[[NCT06630299](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT06630299&esheet=54632375&newsitemid=20261102203384&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT06630299&index=5&md5=875635ea7568cfcef1858e512fddf7c7) \]); and in combination with Merck’s investigational NNRTI ulonivirine (MK-8507) in Phase 2b development (MK-8591B-060 \[[NCT06891066](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT06891066%3Fterm%3DNCT06891066%26viewType%3DCard%26rank%3D1&esheet=54632375&newsitemid=20261102203384&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT06891066&index=6&md5=1feb7f9acb29b0a673d2aa78e1c309bf) \] and MK-8591B-062 \[[NCT07266831](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT07266831%3Fterm%3DNCT07266831%26viewType%3DCard%26rank%3D1&esheet=54632375&newsitemid=20261102203384&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT07266831&index=7&md5=911d9d06249a3a80622617a0c28728de) \]) as a once-weekly oral regimen.


Alimatravir (MK-8527), an investigational once-monthly oral PrEP, is being evaluated in two Phase 3 clinical trials. With financial support from the Gates Foundation, the Phase 3 EXPrESSIVE-10 trial (MK-8527-010,[NCT07071623](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT07071623%3Fterm%3DNCT07071623%26viewType%3DCard%26rank%3D1&esheet=54632375&newsitemid=20261102203384&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT07071623&index=8&md5=3b11f5b5edde5c4ea2d3f277bf431048) ) is evaluating the safety and efficacy of alimatravir in adolescent girls and young women in Kenya, South Africa and Uganda. EXPrESSIVE-11 (MK-8527-011,[NCT07044297](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fclinicaltrials.gov%2Fstudy%2FNCT07044297%3Fterm%3DNCT07044297%26viewType%3DCard%26rank%3D1&esheet=54632375&newsitemid=20261102203384&lan=en-US&anchor=NCT07044297&index=9&md5=ab78dd81f5f9c02655db7d110a058b93) ) is evaluating the safety and efficacy of alimatravir among people with greater likelihood of HIV-1 exposure in 16 countries. Adult enrollment in both trials is now complete.

**Selected Safety Information for IDVYNSO®**


**Contraindications**


IDVYNSO is contraindicated when co-administered with:


- drugs that are strong cytochrome P450 (CYP)3A enzyme inducers as significant decreases in doravirine plasma concentrations may occur, which may decrease the effectiveness of IDVYNSO *.*
- lamivudine (3TC) or emtricitabine (FTC) as significant decreases in islatravir-triphosphate (ISL-TP) concentrations may occur, which may decrease the effectiveness of IDVYNSO. *(See Drug Interactions)*


**Warnings and Precautions**


Severe skin reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS)/toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), have been reported during postmarketing experience with doravirine-containing regimens. In addition, Drug Rash with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS syndrome) was reported with IDVYNSO in a clinical trial. Discontinue IDVYNSO, and other medications associated with these reactions, immediately if a painful rash with mucosal involvement, a progressive severe rash, or a rash with constitutional symptoms, eosinophilia, lymphadenopathy, or other organ involvement develops. Close clinical monitoring and appropriate therapy should be initiated.


The concomitant use of IDVYNSO and certain other drugs may result in known or potentially significant drug interactions, some of which may lead to loss of therapeutic effect of IDVYNSO and possible development of resistance or possible clinically significant adverse reactions from greater exposures of a component of IDVYNSO.


Consider the potential for drug interactions prior to and during IDVYNSO therapy, review concomitant medications during IDVYNSO therapy, and monitor for adverse reactions. *(See Drug Interactions)*


**Adverse Reactions**


The most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥2%, all grades in any treatment group) reported in virologically suppressed participants in the IDVYNSO treatment groups in Trials 051 and 052, respectively, were: diarrhea (3% and 1%), dizziness (2% and 1%), fatigue (2% and 1%), abdominal distension (2% and 1%), headache (2% and 1%) and weight increased (2% and <1%).


A single case of severe immune thrombocytopenia (platelet count nadir of 2 x109/L) characterized by abrupt onset of subcutaneous hematoma, petechiae, and hematuria was reported in a participant 32 days after initiating IDVYNSO. ** The case resolved with discontinuation of IDVYNSO, in conjunction with treatments including corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Among all participants in Trials 052 and 051, there were no patterns of platelet decreases over time with IDVYNSO and no differences between treatment arms in mean change from baseline in platelet count.


**Drug Interactions**


IDVYNSO is a complete regimen; co-administration with other antiretroviral medications for treatment of HIV-1 infection is not recommended.


Co-administration of IDVYNSO with a CYP3A inducer decreases doravirine plasma concentrations, which may reduce the efficacy of IDVYNSO. If IDVYNSO is co-administered with rifabutin, one tablet of doravirine should be taken approximately 12 hours after the dose of IDVYNSO. Co-administration of IDVYNSO with other moderate CYP3A inducers is not recommended.


Co-administration of IDVYNSO and drugs that are inhibitors of CYP3A may result in increased plasma concentrations of doravirine.


Co-administration of IDVYNSO is not recommended with deoxycytidine kinase (dCK) substrates (e.g., nucleoside antimetabolites) as they may reduce the exposure of islatravir-triphosphate or with adenosine deaminase (ADA) inhibitors (e.g., pentostatin) as they may increase the exposure of islatravir. *(See Contraindications)*


**Use in Specific Populations**


There are insufficient human data on the use of IDVYNSO during pregnancy to inform a drug-associated risk of birth defects and miscarriage. Healthcare providers are encouraged to call the Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry (APR) at 1-800-258-4263 to report pregnancy outcomes in individuals exposed to IDVYNSO.


It is unknown whether IDVYNSO or any of its components are present in human milk, affects human milk production, or has effects on the breastfed infant. Inform patients that the potential risks of breastfeeding include: (1) HIV-1 transmission (in infants without HIV-1), (2) developing viral resistance (in infants with HIV-1), and (3) serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant similar to those seen in adults.


Clinical trials in virologically suppressed participants who received IDVYNSO included 81 (11%) participants aged 65 years and older, including 10 (1%) aged 75 years and older. Overall differences in response have not been identified between the elderly and younger patients, but greater sensitivity of some older individuals cannot be ruled out.


No dosage adjustment of IDVYNSO is required in patients with eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m2. IDVYNSO is not recommended in patients with eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2 and has not been studied in participants undergoing dialysis.


No dosage adjustment of IDVYNSO is recommended in patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class A or B). IDVYNSO has not been studied in patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C) and therefore is not recommended in these patients.


IDVYNSO does not have activity against hepatitis B virus (HBV). Patients with HBV coinfection who switch to IDVYNSO from an antiretroviral regimen with activity against HBV, and patients on IDVYNSO who are newly diagnosed with HBV coinfection, should be closely monitored and specific anti-HBV therapy should be considered, as clinically appropriate.
